education.disclaimer: General educational visualization. This model does not represent the patient's actual eye. Only an appropriate healthcare professional can determine whether these changes are present.
education.progression_limit: These four teaching views are simplified examples, not a clinical staging system, a prediction, or an inevitable sequence. Never assign a view to a patient from a follow-up signal.

sources.title: Vision Loss and Diabetes
sources.publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

anatomy.title: Retina
anatomy.text: At the back of the eye, the retina turns incoming light into signals used for vision.

anatomy.title: Macula
anatomy.text: The macula is the retinal area used for sharp central vision.

anatomy.title: Retinal blood vessels
anatomy.text: Diabetes can damage the small retinal vessels, affecting blood flow and allowing fluid or blood to escape.

anatomy.title: Optic nerve
anatomy.text: Signals from the retina travel along the optic nerve to the brain.

anatomy.title: Cornea
anatomy.text: The clear front surface bends incoming light to help focus it.

anatomy.title: Lens
anatomy.text: Inside the eye, the lens helps focus light onto the retina.

follow_up.title: Why follow-up matters
follow_up.text: Diabetes-related retinal changes can begin without noticeable symptoms. A dilated eye examination lets an eye professional check the retina. A record reminder is a reason to clarify documented follow-up, not evidence that someone has retinal disease.

states.title: Normal educational view
states.text: This reference view introduces retinal anatomy and visual signalling. It does not establish that a particular person's eyes are healthy.

states.title: General early changes
states.text: In early diabetic retinopathy, small vessel walls may weaken and bulge. People may not notice symptoms.

states.title: General progressing changes
states.text: Fluid leaking from damaged vessels can cause swelling in the macula and affect central vision. This example is not a separate formal disease stage.

states.title: General advanced changes
states.text: Advanced proliferative disease can involve fragile new vessels that bleed. This is a general example, not a forecast for any patient.
